t: You're facing the Shepherd Gate Clock, mounted on the wall outside the gate of the Royal Observatory in Greenwich. Look at the dial: it shows all twenty-four hours, rather than twelve. Charles Shepherd built and installed a network of electrically controlled clocks in 1852, and this one was probably the first to show Greenwich Mean Time to the public. It is a sympathetic clock, driven by electric pulses from a motor clock inside the main building. Originally it showed astronomical time, which began at noon rather than midnight.
